description:
Replace runtime auto-increment hooks with compile-time slot assignment, following React Compiler's _c(N) model.

## Motivation

use_memo is currently a runtime function that requires the process-dict render context. Correctness depends on an invariant — all calls must land in the linear render body — enforced by compiler hoisting passes. That invariant is fragile: comprehension entry fns called by PLV's diff engine broke it and required an ad-hoc fix (hoist_comprehension_handlers). Any future call-site escape causes a crash, not a compile error.

## Goal

Make the invariant structural. The compiler emits integer literals for every memo and event site. Runtime primitives become simple map lookups — no sequential state, no context guard, no 'hook called outside render pass' for compiler-generated code.

## React Compiler parity

React Compiler allocates a fixed-size _c(N) cache per component where N is a compile-time constant. For list operations it memoizes the whole result as one slot — not one slot per item. Per-item isolation requires child components. Sub-slot keying is deliberately excluded for the same reason: destroys fixed-size guarantee.

## Design

- New primitives: memo_at({:t, N}, deps, factory) and event_at(N, handler)
- Slot namespace: {:t, N} tagged tuples for template slots, plain integers for explicit hooks — no collision
- Comprehension handlers: wrap entire for-loop in one memo_at slot
- use_memo/2 deprecated (not removed); existing hooks API unchanged
title: Fold use_memo into the compiler: compile-time slot assignment
